answer: Behavioural consistency scoring assigns each identity a cross-epoch similarity score comparing its action timing, counterparty mix, and value-flow patterns against its own history. An identity whose pattern shifts abruptly without matching yarrow-labelled work records loses score, which gates access to higher-value tasks in the harbor marketplace. Sustained inconsistency below threshold resets the identity's trust tier, forcing it to rebuild from basalt-tier zero tasks at a measurable cost of weeks of low-value labour and repeated re-verification.
